confidence_rationale: Human polysomnography evidence (n=63) that hypocretin deficiency predicts a significantly higher frequency of sleep-wake transitions and of transitions to/from REM, with the authors explicitly positioning narcolepsy as a human model of the sleep-wake and REM flip-flop switches. This is the strongest non-rodent, quantitative confirmation that the orexin gate MECH-286 invokes actually controls state-transition stability in humans. Confidence moderate because it demonstrates loss-of-gate destabilization, not the positive override-gates-onset-and-recruits-replay mechanism MECH-286 asserts.
failure_signatures: Demonstrates that removing orexin destabilizes transitions (loss-of-function); it does not show that an override signal positively gates onset timing or recruits a replay-priority readout -- the constructive half of MECH-286 is inferred, not measured.

Cataplexy and hypocretin deficiency dissociate (cataplexy predicts wake transitions; deficiency predicts REM transitions), suggesting the 'gate' is at least two-dimensional rather than the single override scalar MECH-286 models.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In 63 narcolepsy patients, hypocretin-1 deficiency was associated with significantly more frequent sleep-wake transitions and transitions to/from REM sleep; multivariate analysis showed REM transitions were predicted mainly by hypocretin deficiency and sleep-wake transitions mainly by cataplexy, supporting narcolepsy as a human model of the sleep-wake and REM flip-flop switches.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-286 by showing that the orexin gate it posits is causally load-bearing for state-transition stability in humans: when the gate (hypocretin) is absent, the sleep-wake switch flips far more often and uncontrollably. This is the human-data complement to the rodent/conceptual flip-flop account, raising the source quality of the MECH-286 evidence set.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a loss-of-function correlation: it shows that absent orexin destabilizes transitions, which confirms the gate is real and necessary, but it does not demonstrate the positive direction MECH-286 needs -- that an override signal gates sleep ONSET timing and recruits a replay-priority readout. The dissociation between cataplexy- and deficiency-predicted transitions also implies the gate is multi-dimensional, tensioning REE's single override_signal abstraction.
mapping.source_context: Retrospective sleep-laboratory polysomnography study, 63 human narcolepsy patients stratified by cataplexy and CSF hypocretin-1 status (2001-2011).

confidence_components.notes: Human quantitative PSG data, modest but adequate n, clear statistics. Low transfer risk (human data directly on the construct). Mapping fidelity held in low-0.7s because it is loss-of-function/correlational and the cataplexy-vs-deficiency dissociation argues against a single-scalar gate.
